page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text, with an indented verse stanza in its middle and a Greek passage at the foot of the column. No marginal notes. Show-through and the scan edge on the left are not printed text.

main_text.p: his laboriosis exercitationibus & dolor intercurrit nonnunquam: feriuntur, im-pelluntur, abjiciuntur, cadunt: & ipsè labor quasi callum obducit dolori. Prolixius Xenophon & Plutarchus: & eleganter Propertius elegiar. lib. iii.

p.i: Multa tua, Sparte, miramur jura palestra, Sed mage virginei tot bona gymnasii: Quod non infames exercet corpore laudes, Inter luctantes nuda puella viros, Cum pila veloces fallit per brachia jactus, Increpat & versi clavis adunca trochi. Pulverulentaque ad extremas stat fœmina metas, Et patitur duro vulnera pancratio. Nunc ligat ad caestum[?] gaudentia brachia loris, Missile nunc disci pondus in orbe rotat.

main_text.p: Et Lycurgus instituti hujus autor interrogatus, cur corpora virginum cursu, lucta, disci & jaculi jactu exerceret, Græcis verbis respondit: ἵνα ἡ τ᾽ γυναικῶν ῥώμην ῥίζωσις[?] ἰσχυρὸν ἐν ἰσχύροις σώ- ζειν [illegible, ~8 letters] ἡαλᾶς βλαστά[?] νῆ[?]

page.notes: The Greek passage is a faint, small scan and is only partly legible; its words are uncertain and marked [?] or illegible. The text of the verse follows the printed spelling as far as I can read it; "caestum" and "mage" are doubtful. Show-through from the reverse side appears at the lower left and must not be transcribed. The printed heading and the text at the top left have no further marks.
